summary.intent: Apply a set of pending fixes in the caliper repo: a heap-meter fix, a private-name fix, and resolving the merge conflict on PR #509 (change 307), each in its own git worktree.
summary.outcome: The #509 conflict was resolved by merging main and pushed as 58d84343; GitHub reports it MERGEABLE but BLOCKED. The heap-meter fix has a passing regression test (verified by mutation) and a changeset, but its lint gate failed and was not investigated. The private-name fix has not been started.

repo: Fixes are done in per-task git worktrees under .claude/worktrees/ created from origin/main (e.g. heap-meter, merge-509).
A fresh worktree needs `pnpm install` before JS-dependent workspace tests or lint checks will pass; the missing install caused a spurious test failure on the merge.
Changes ship with a changeset file in .changeset/ (e.g. heap-meter-below-zero.md).

Test and lint commands: `cargo check --all-targets`, `cargo nextest run --workspace --no-fail-fast`, `just test-checker-lane`, and `just lint doc-check machete typos`; CI also runs the checker lane and lint gate.
A commit hook runs on commit in this repo.
The conflict in `composes` in crates/semantic/src/convert.rs came from #506 and #508 landing; resolution kept #509's cached `alias_arguments` and #506's `below_react` flag.

code.finding: The heap meter's committed() accounting used a plain cast that went below zero; the fix replaced it, and a new test fails when the plain cast is restored (mutation-verified).
Single merge conflict in `composes`, resolved by combining #509's `alias_arguments` caching with #506's `below_react` flag.

workflow: Verify a regression test by temporarily restoring the buggy code and confirming the test fails (mutation proof).
Distinguish environmental failures (missing pnpm install) from real regressions by reading the failure output before blaming the change.
Merging main into a PR branch to resolve conflicts, then checking GitHub mergeability, avoids rewriting history.
